quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, you must show:
questions.explanation: You must have your driver's license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance in your vehicle at all times. Officers can ask you to show all three documents.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check for vehicles.

questions.explanation: Check both mirrors for traffic behind you. Then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving into the other lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to hazards ahead. This sign tells you that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let them merge safely.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices used in work zones?
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Use extra caution when you see orange warning devices on the road.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, you should:

options.text: Make a quick turn from your lane.
Drive to the next exit or safe place to turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the next exit or safe place to turn around.
questions.explanation: Never back up on a freeway or shoulder. Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: When should you use a sharp blast of your horn?

options.text: When a driver ahead is going under the speed limit.
When you exit an alley and cannot see ahead.
When another vehicle is about to hit you.
When you want to pass another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When another vehicle is about to hit you.
questions.explanation: Use a sharp horn blast only in real danger—such as when a collision might happen. A light tap is better for other situations. Do not use your horn to rush other drivers.

questions.question: When driving near a blind person with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and yield. Be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, slow down for turns and curves. This is especially important because tires have less grip in these conditions.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Look behind and to both sides of your vehicle before turning. Slow down to turn safely.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about conditions ahead that may be dangerous. These might include a sharp turn, steep hill, or other hazard. You need to be ready to act.

questions.question: What does this road sign show?

options.text: The maximum safe speed for a residential area.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway entrance.
The maximum safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the recommended maximum speed for leaving a highway. In this example, the speed is 30 mph.

questions.question: What is a distraction when driving?

options.text: Anything that causes you to swerve while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that pulls your focus away from driving. Distractions can happen anywhere and at any time. They can cause crashes, injuries, and death.

questions.question: How should you change lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you plan to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, turn on your signal. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Make sure no one else is moving into the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing red or blue lights?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before it catches up to you.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let all emergency vehicles pass. Move to the right edge of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: What can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
questions.explanation: As more drivers use the roads, road rage becomes more common. To prevent it, use turn signals, follow speed limits, and leave yourself extra time to reach your destination.

questions.question: What is true about traffic signs and pavement markings?

options.text: They must be followed only when there is other traffic.
They must be followed only when a police officer is present.

questions.explanation: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and keep drivers safe. You must always obey them.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers must focus on driving. For every mile driven, a driver makes about 200 decisions. Any other task can be a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: What must you do when you leave your vehicle unattended?

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: What should you do before turning?
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Do what other cars are doing, even if the crossing guard says otherwise.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when a sign, crossing guard, or police officer tells you to. Always drive with extra caution in school zones.

questions.question: Just like alcohol and other drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep causes poor driving. Like drugs and alcohol, sleepiness slows your reactions, lowers your awareness, and affects your judgment.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Adjust your speed to avoid brake damage or crashes.

questions.question: An intersection has no traffic signs or signals. You arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. You should:

options.text: Speed up and go through the intersection.
Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
Drive into the intersection and force the other vehicle to stop.
Honk your horn and drive through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the vehicle on your right go first.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Wait for that vehicle to pass safely before you go.

questions.question: The effect of lack of sleep on your driving ability is the same as:

options.text: The effect of driving with teenagers.

questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol impair your driving the same way. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving about as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.05 percent. Being awake for 24 hours affects driving about the same as a blood alcohol level of 0.10 percent.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Pedestrians are walking along the road.
Be alert for construction workers on the road.

questions.explanation: This sign warns of a pedestrian crossing ahead. Drive carefully where pedestrians might be present.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Traffic only moves in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic only moves in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: This one-way sign shows that traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: If a traffic light is green and a police officer tells you to stop, you should:

options.text: Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.explanation: Always obey a police officer's instructions, even if they conflict with traffic laws, signs, signals, or road markings.

questions.question: "No passing zone" signs tell drivers:
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass other vehicles in that area. These signs are used where visibility is poor and passing would be unsafe.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle. You should:

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop whenever you see pedestrians on or crossing the road. Be extra careful around children. Always let pedestrians cross in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?

options.text: It makes the driver worry about the cost of the call.
It takes up the driver's hands, eyes, and attention.
It distracts other drivers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes up the driver's hands, eyes, and attention.
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous. It takes up your hands, eyes, and mind. Even skilled drivers are more likely to crash when using a cell phone.

questions.question: What is a good way to avoid getting tired on a long trip?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Take a short break every two hours on a long trip to avoid fatigue. If you feel drowsy, pull over to a safe place and take a nap or stay somewhere for the night.

questions.question: What is the best way to change lanes?

options.text: When a car is in your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and carefully. Only change lanes when needed. Each lane change increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in work zones?

options.text: Follow the car in front of you closely.
Pass the car in front of you as soon as possible.
Keep a safe distance and do not follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and do not follow too closely.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, stay far away from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other cars. Keep more space between your car and others. Do not tailgate.

questions.question: When a blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street, what should you do?

options.text: You must always let them cross first.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only need to let them cross if you are at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always let them cross first.
questions.explanation: Blind or partially blind pedestrians use a white cane or guide dog. You must always let these pedestrians cross first.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing your lane but there is no crosswalk. What should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact and then pass them.
Slow down as you pass them.
Stop and let them finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them finish crossing.
questions.explanation: At any intersection, you must let pedestrians cross first, even if there is no marked crosswalk. Always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians cross first.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should let you go first.
Never let oncoming traffic and pedestrians cross first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: When turning left, let cars going straight cross first. Always let pedestrians cross first.

questions.question: When a police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, what should drivers do?

options.text: Watch what other cars are doing.

questions.explanation: Traffic lights help keep traffic moving and prevent crashes. Drivers must follow traffic lights and obey officers when they are directing traffic.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what headlights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams bounce off the weather and make it harder to see.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while driving?

options.text: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired, stop to rest or change drivers. Tiredness slows your thinking and reactions, which makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: Before you start the car, you should:

options.text: Make sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.

questions.explanation: Make a habit of buckling your safety belt before you start the car. Make sure all passengers buckle theirs too.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: When weather changes suddenly, change your driving.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles behind you during bad weather.

questions.explanation: When the weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Slow down in rain and fog. Pay attention to vehicles behind you that may be driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a roundabout is ahead. Enter a roundabout slowly and let the cars already in it go first.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate:

options.text: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or try to turn around on the highway if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit and safely turn around.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle when:

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross it to change lanes. A solid line means you cannot cross it. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: Braking distance is affected by:

options.text: How fast your vehicle is traveling.
The condition of your brakes and tires.

questions.explanation: How long it takes to stop depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
Only dangerous to the driver who drinks.

questions.explanation: Driving after drinking alcohol is very dangerous. You cannot drive safely after drinking. It puts you and everyone on the road at risk.

questions.question: If one of your tires blows out while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Steer straight and slowly remove your foot from the gas pedal.
Keep your current speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert traffic behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer straight and slowly remove your foot from the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Ease off the gas pedal. Do not brake hard. Once you have control, brake gently and pull over safely.

questions.question: A sign of a drunk driver is:
questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include weaving, driving slower than traffic, jerky motions, and sudden stops.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, you should:

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show they are wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get out of their way. Do not try to get even with them. This only makes the situation more dangerous.
